# lean-run

Carry the request through its authorized endpoint. Follow project instructions, preserve unrelated work and reuse verified context. This skill works alone; companions are optional and no Lean runtime or workflow directory is required.

## Settle scope, then act

Read applicable instructions and the nearest relevant source/tests in one focused pass. Record outcome, observable acceptance, constraints, verification and destination; a sentence suffices for a bounded change. Use standard procedure depth unless requested otherwise; depth does not select model settings. For broad ambiguity read [exploration](references/exploration.md); skip discovery loops for clear requests or an instruction to proceed. Ask only indispensable missing decisions and continue independent work. Silence is not consent.

Resolve consequential business rules, permissions, data lifecycle and external contracts before implementation. Decide reversible details from project conventions. Implementation authorization includes matching preparation and verification without another plan approval. Requested PRs/deployments remain acceptance and require matching authority/tools; finish preparation before any necessary final approval. End-to-end work grants no extra publishing, spending or provider permissions. Create workflow files only when requested. On pause, handoff or cross-session resume read [continuation](references/handoff.md).

## Use the smallest complete procedure

Reuse or classify risk as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH and quality as STANDARD/HIGH/VERY_HIGH. Consequential security, destructive data and breaking external contracts are HIGH risk. Before implementing or reviewing persistent, concurrent or access-scoped **application data** writes, read [write integrity](references/write-integrity.md).

For a bounded implementation, settle a short requirement-to-evidence map and make the smallest complete edit. Prefer verified project/library primitives. Reproduce a fault with one targeted batch before repair; a full baseline suite is useful only when required or needed to locate it. Write compact checks for actual gaps. Use test-first development when requested; ordinary work does not require building a comprehensive new suite before the edit. Expand investigation for a demonstrated failure or unresolved requirement.

After the edit, run affected and required checks on final content, exercise the relevant public journey with important failures, and review the complete diff including new files. Reuse passing evidence whose inputs and relevant environment remain unchanged. Do not repeat whole suites to confirm a clear completion summary. A check proves only its mapped acceptance; unit tests, builds and mocks do not establish an untested live integration. Record actions, environment, expected/observed results and simulated boundaries. Disclose unavailable reproduction or live access and report remaining acceptance.

Use existing VCS diffs when available. Otherwise save one temporary copy of files before editing and compare with it; inspect added files separately. Keep source on disk: do not print base64/serialized copies merely to reconstruct a later diff. Read a source once, then changed sections. Batch independent reads/checks and serialize dependent work.

For **assessment-only** work, inspect contract, current source/diff and tests; run required checks once, then independently probe remaining boundary/failure risks through the public interface. Do not recreate a comprehensive suite or alternative implementation when inspected source and verified tests establish the behavior. Expand for a concrete gap or contradiction. Reproduce old failures only to establish a finding or when requested. Assessment does not authorize implementation or delivery.

## Review and repair

LOW permits an acceptance self-check; MEDIUM needs focused correctness/regression review; HIGH needs a fresh independent reviewer. Quality HIGH requires at least MEDIUM review; VERY_HIGH requires HIGH. A reviewer inspects current source and runs independent checks; author conclusions cannot supply independence. Unavailable required independence is BLOCKED.

Derive equivalence classes and boundary/failure cases from acceptance. Extend to exhaustive/random sweeps only for an identified gap or hypothesis; case count alone is not evidence. Repair demonstrated in-scope failures, rerun affected checks and renew review of changed content. Verify integrated worker results. Stop once mandatory coverage and findings are resolved.

Count review REWORK across the entire task, companions, workers and resumes. After the second REWORK, allow one final fix-only pass plus verification/review; unresolved mandatory findings mean FAILED. Never reset counts through nested workflows. Each repair needs new evidence/hypothesis and a distinguishing check; abandon approaches yielding no new information. Suspected flaky checks permit at most two disclosed unchanged retries. Never weaken acceptance, disable checks or omit mandatory work for speed. Separate unrelated failures and seek direction only if repairing them expands scope.

## Load procedures only when useful

Read an available companion only when its procedure helps the remaining work; pass settled scope and relevant raw evidence. If absent, perform the core procedure here. Missing a skill is not a blocker; a required capability can be.

| Need | Optional companion |
| --- | --- |
| Repository, conventions, agent instructions | `lean-target`, `lean-init`, `lean-instructions` |
| Scope, decisions, research | `lean-scope`, `lean-grill`, `lean-research` |
| Implementation, useful delegation | `lean-task`, `lean-agents` |
| Review, completion evidence | `lean-review`, `lean-gate` |
| Security, authorized release/recovery | `lean-security`, `lean-release` |
| Requested depth or skill/model update | `lean-effort`, `lean-update`, `lean-model-update` |

This workflow requests selective delegation when useful or required for independence, subject to host/user restrictions. Keep small work inline; default to one active worker, with more only for explicit parallel work. Before dispatch read [delegation](references/delegation.md). One controller owns scope, integration, repair counts and delivery.

For noisy suites or expected failures, execute the bundled [check runner](scripts/check.py): `python3 /resolved/skill/path/scripts/check.py -- COMMAND ARG...`. It retains full stdout/stderr, returns the command exit status and emits a bounded excerpt. No default timeout; optional `--timeout SECONDS`; `--log NEW_PATH` refuses overwrite. Execute it without reading its implementation unless debugging/changing it. Small bounded checks can run directly. If Python is unavailable, use equivalent host capture without installing a runtime. Inspect saved logs for failures or ambiguous completion until distinct causes are understood; keep full logs accessible and never hide failures.

## Deliver with evidence

For user-facing work include affected accessibility, keyboard/focus, screen sizes and loading/empty/error/recovery states. Performance work needs a representative workload and measured baseline before optimization; a proposal alone does not authorize benchmarking. Security work maps protected data, entry points, trust transitions and permissions, then probes relevant abuse cases. Releases check artifact/environment, dependencies/configuration/migration compatibility, health criteria and authorized recovery before mutation; verify deployment and observation. Inspect uncertain state before retrying. Application rollback grants no destructive data-restore authority; a failed release followed by recovery remains a failed release.

Advance when evidence is sufficient and reopen decisions only for new requirements or contradictions. Match every acceptance item, including delivery, to current commands/actions and outcomes, review coverage and limits. DONE requires all mandatory acceptance, verification, review and the authorized destination. Otherwise report BLOCKED or FAILED, completed work, affected acceptance and the exact next action. A plan, worker report or stage PASS does not complete unfinished work. Keep updates/final concise; do not ask to continue authorized work. These procedures are not enforced hooks or a guarantee of success.

Repair vault.py and app.py for a LOCAL SYNTHETIC accounting fixture.
No real payments, identity provider, production data or deployment.
The tenant argument is trusted authenticated context supplied by a
caller; implementing authentication is outside scope. Every account
read and both ends of a transfer MUST be within that tenant.
Public API: init_db(path); balance(path,tenant,account) -> int;
transfer(path,tenant,source,target,amount,key) -> receipt containing
tenant,key,source,target,amount. Keep the existing accounts,
transfers and audit table names and columns; preserve existing rows.
Account identity is (tenant,name). A nonempty tenant/account/key
string and distinct existing source/target are required. Amount is
a positive integer excluding bool. Reject malformed requests,
insufficient funds and key conflicts with ValueError without writes.
Missing and inaccessible accounts have the same generic error and
reveal no other tenant's details. Read isolation also applies to
cached transfer receipts. Keys are scoped to tenant: exact replay
returns the original receipt with no changes, a different payload
conflicts, and another tenant can independently use the same key.
Debit, credit, transfer receipt and one audit row are ONE transaction.
A storage/audit failure propagates and leaves all four unchanged.
With separate simultaneous connections, duplicate same-key requests
all return the same receipt, execute once, and create one audit row.
Concurrent distinct-key requests never overspend or lose credits.
Atomicity/deduplication must survive reopening the database.
Existing schema has accounts(tenant,name,balance),
transfers(tenant,key,source,target,amount), and audit with the same
columns as transfers. Do not remove audit triggers to bypass failures.
CLI: python3 -B app.py DB JSON_REQUEST. Operations are balance with
tenant/account, or transfer with tenant/source/target/amount/key.
Valid calls print one JSON result and exit 0. Invalid calls exit 2,
emit no stdout, and write a generic JSON error on stderr without a
traceback, SQL statement or another tenant's information.
Use only Python/SQLite standard libraries. Delivery is local files.
Fresh independent final review is required and supplied separately
by the benchmark coordinator. Do not claim it before it occurs.

import json
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from contextlib import closing
from pathlib import Path

import vault


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
TABLES = ('accounts', 'transfers', 'audit')


class VaultRegressionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.path = self.new_db('vault')

    def new_db(self, name):
        path = Path(self.tmp.name) / f'{name}.sqlite'
        vault.init_db(path)
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(path)) as con, con:
            con.executemany(
                'INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
                [('one', 'a', 100), ('one', 'b', 0),
                 ('two', 'a', 700), ('two', 'b', 40),
                 ('two', 'private', 900)],
            )
        return path

    def snapshot(self, path=None):
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(path or self.path)) as con:
            return {table: con.execute(
                f'SELECT * FROM {table} ORDER BY '
                + ('1, 2, 3' if table == 'accounts' else '1, 2, 3, 4, 5')
            ).fetchall() for table in TABLES}

    def sql(self, script, path=None):
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(path or self.path)) as con:
            con.executescript(script)

    def cli(self, request):
        return self.command(str(self.path), json.dumps(request))

    def command(self, *arguments):
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'app.py'), *arguments],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT, timeout=15,
        )

    def history(self, path):
        return [vault.transfer(path, tenant, 'a', 'b', 9, f'past_{tenant}')
                for tenant in ('one', 'two')]

    def check_history_replay(self, path, receipts):
        before = self.snapshot(path)
        vault.init_db(path)
        for receipt in receipts:
            self.assertEqual(vault.transfer(path, **receipt), receipt)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(path), before)

    def concurrent(self, path, requests):
        barrier = threading.Barrier(len(requests))

        def run(request):
            barrier.wait(timeout=5)
            try:
                return vault.transfer(path, **request)
            except ValueError as error:
                return error

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(requests)) as pool:
            futures = [pool.submit(run, request) for request in requests]
            return [future.result(timeout=20) for future in futures]

    def test_balance_is_scoped_and_missing_is_generic(self):
        self.assertEqual(vault.balance(self.path, 'two', 'a'), 700)
        errors = []
        for account in ('private', 'missing'):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as raised:
                vault.balance(self.path, 'one', account)
            errors.append(str(raised.exception))
        self.assertEqual(errors[0], errors[1])
        self.assertNotIn('private', errors[0])
        self.assertNotIn('two', errors[0])

    def test_transfer_is_scoped_and_replay_is_payload_bound(self):
        before = self.snapshot()
        receipt = vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'shared')
        self.assertEqual(receipt, dict(
            tenant='one', key='shared', source='a', target='b', amount=10))
        after = self.snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(after['accounts'], [
            ('one', 'a', 90), ('one', 'b', 10), *before['accounts'][2:]])
        self.assertEqual(
            vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'shared'), receipt)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), after)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 11, 'shared')
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), after)
        other = vault.transfer(self.path, 'two', 'a', 'b', 20, 'shared')
        self.assertEqual(other['tenant'], 'two')
        self.assertEqual(vault.balance(self.path, 'two', 'a'), 680)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.snapshot()['audit']), 2)

    def test_audit_failure_rolls_back_every_effect(self):
        self.sql("""
            CREATE TRIGGER fail_audit BEFORE INSERT ON audit BEGIN
              SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'private storage details');
            END;
        """)
        before = self.snapshot()
        with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
            vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'failure')
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)

    def test_cli_errors_are_generic_json(self):
        before = self.snapshot()
        result = self.cli(dict(op='balance', tenant='one', account='private'))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, '')
        error = json.loads(result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(set(error), {'error'})
        self.assertNotIn('private', result.stderr)
        self.assertNotIn('two', result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)

    def test_invalid_inputs_are_rejected_without_writes(self):
        valid = dict(tenant='one', source='a', target='b', amount=10, key='new')
        invalid = [dict(valid, **{field: value})
                   for field in ('tenant', 'source', 'target', 'key')
                   for value in ('', None, 1, True, b'a', [], {})]
        invalid += [dict(valid, amount=value)
                    for value in (0, -1, True, False, 1.0, '1', None, [], {})]
        invalid += [dict(valid, target='a'), dict(valid, amount=101),
                    dict(valid, amount=2**100)]
        before = self.snapshot()
        for request in invalid:
            with self.subTest(request=request):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    vault.transfer(self.path, **request)
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)
        for field in ('tenant', 'account'):
            for value in ('', None, 1, True, [], {}):
                with self.subTest(field=field, value=value):
                    request = dict(tenant='one', account='a')
                    request[field] = value
                    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                        vault.balance(self.path, **request)
                    self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)

    def test_missing_or_inaccessible_transfer_ends_are_generic(self):
        before = self.snapshot()
        messages = []
        for field in ('source', 'target'):
            for account in ('private', 'missing', "a' OR 1=1 --"):
                with self.subTest(field=field, account=account):
                    request = dict(tenant='one', source='a', target='b',
                                   amount=10, key='missing')
                    request[field] = account
                    with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as raised:
                        vault.transfer(self.path, **request)
                    messages.append(str(raised.exception))
                    self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as raised:
            vault.balance(self.path, 'unknown', 'a')
        messages.append(str(raised.exception))
        self.assertEqual(len(set(messages)), 1)
        self.assertFalse(any(word in messages[0] for word in ('two', 'private', '900')))

    def test_replay_checks_every_payload_field_and_needs_no_funds(self):
        request = dict(tenant='one', source='a', target='b', amount=100, key='all')
        receipt = vault.transfer(self.path, **request)
        self.assertEqual(vault.balance(self.path, 'one', 'a'), 0)
        after = self.snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(vault.transfer(self.path, **request), receipt)
        for change in ({'amount': 99}, {'source': 'missing'},
                       {'target': 'missing'}, {'source': 'b', 'target': 'a'}):
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    vault.transfer(self.path, **dict(request, **change))
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), after)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            vault.transfer(self.path, **dict(request, key='different'))
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), after)

    def test_init_preserves_schema_rows_and_triggers(self):
        self.history(self.path)
        self.sql('CREATE TRIGGER retained AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN SELECT 1; END;')
        before = self.snapshot()
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(self.path)) as con:
            schema = con.execute('SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master ORDER BY name').fetchall()
        vault.init_db(self.path)
        vault.init_db(self.path)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(self.path)) as con:
            self.assertEqual(con.execute(
                'SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master ORDER BY name'
            ).fetchall(), schema)

    def test_integer_boundaries_and_literal_identifiers(self):
        maximum = 2**63 - 1
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(self.path)) as con, con:
            con.execute('UPDATE accounts SET balance=? WHERE tenant=? AND name=?',
                        (maximum, 'one', 'a'))
            con.executemany('INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (?, ?, ?)', [
                ("tenant' --", ' ', 1), ("tenant' --", '雪', 0)])
        receipt = vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', maximum, 'maximum')
        self.assertIs(type(vault.balance(self.path, 'one', 'b')), int)
        self.assertEqual(vault.balance(self.path, 'one', 'b'), maximum)
        self.assertEqual(vault.transfer(self.path, **receipt), receipt)
        strange = vault.transfer(self.path, "tenant' --", ' ', '雪', 1, "key' --")
        self.assertEqual(vault.transfer(self.path, **strange), strange)

    def test_credit_overflow_rolls_back(self):
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(self.path)) as con, con:
            con.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance=? WHERE tenant='one' AND name='b'",
                        (2**63 - 1,))
        before = self.snapshot()
        with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
            vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 1, 'overflow')
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)

    def test_malformed_other_tenant_data_does_not_affect_requests(self):
        self.sql("""
            UPDATE accounts SET balance='private nonnumeric balance' WHERE tenant='two';
            INSERT INTO transfers VALUES ('two', 'shared', 'private', 'secret', 'bad amount');
            INSERT INTO audit VALUES ('two', 'shared', NULL, 'secret', X'ABCD');
        """)
        before = self.snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(vault.balance(self.path, 'one', 'a'), 100)
        receipt = vault.transfer(self.path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'shared')
        self.assertEqual(receipt['tenant'], 'one')
        after = self.snapshot()
        for table in TABLES:
            self.assertEqual([row for row in after[table] if row[0] == 'two'],
                             [row for row in before[table] if row[0] == 'two'])

    def test_storage_failures_at_each_stage_roll_back(self):
        triggers = [
            "BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts WHEN OLD.tenant='one' AND OLD.name='b'",
            'BEFORE INSERT ON transfers',
            'AFTER INSERT ON transfers',
            'BEFORE INSERT ON audit',
            'AFTER INSERT ON audit',
        ]
        for index, clause in enumerate(triggers):
            for action in ('ABORT', 'FAIL', 'ROLLBACK'):
                with self.subTest(clause=clause, action=action):
                    path = self.new_db(f'failure-{index}-{action}')
                    receipts = self.history(path)
                    self.sql(f"""CREATE TRIGGER fault {clause} BEGIN
                        SELECT RAISE({action}, 'private storage details'); END;""", path)
                    before = self.snapshot(path)
                    with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
                        vault.transfer(path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'failed')
                    self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(path), before)
                    self.check_history_replay(path, receipts)
                    with closing(sqlite3.connect(path)) as con:
                        self.assertIsNotNone(con.execute(
                            "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger' AND name='fault'"
                        ).fetchone())

    def test_silent_missing_or_wrong_effects_roll_back(self):
        scripts = [
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts
               WHEN OLD.tenant='one' AND OLD.name='a' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END;""",
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts
               WHEN OLD.tenant='one' AND OLD.name='b' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END;""",
            'CREATE TRIGGER fault BEFORE INSERT ON transfers BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END;',
            'CREATE TRIGGER fault BEFORE INSERT ON audit BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END;',
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN
               UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance+1 WHERE tenant='one' AND name='b'; END;""",
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN
               UPDATE transfers SET amount=amount+1 WHERE tenant=NEW.tenant AND key=NEW.key; END;""",
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN
               UPDATE audit SET amount=amount+1 WHERE rowid=NEW.rowid; END;""",
            """CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN
               INSERT INTO audit VALUES(NEW.tenant,NEW.key,NEW.source,NEW.target,NEW.amount); END;""",
        ]
        for index, script in enumerate(scripts):
            with self.subTest(script=script):
                path = self.new_db(f'silent-{index}')
                self.sql(script, path)
                before = self.snapshot(path)
                with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
                    vault.transfer(path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'new')
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(path), before)

    def test_unrelated_accounts_and_history_cannot_change(self):
        statements = [
            "DELETE FROM accounts WHERE tenant='two' AND name='private'",
            "UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance+1 WHERE tenant='two' AND name='b'",
            "INSERT INTO accounts VALUES('two','unexpected',1)",
            "DELETE FROM transfers WHERE tenant='one' AND key='past_one'",
            "DELETE FROM transfers WHERE tenant='two' AND key='past_two'",
            "UPDATE transfers SET amount=amount+1 WHERE tenant='two'",
            "INSERT INTO transfers VALUES('one','unexpected','a','b',1)",
            "DELETE FROM audit WHERE tenant='one' AND key='past_one'",
            "UPDATE audit SET amount=amount+1 WHERE tenant='two'",
            "INSERT INTO audit SELECT * FROM audit WHERE tenant='two'",
        ]
        for index, statement in enumerate(statements):
            with self.subTest(statement=statement):
                path = self.new_db(f'unrelated-{index}')
                receipts = self.history(path)
                self.sql(f'CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN {statement}; END;', path)
                before = self.snapshot(path)
                with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
                    vault.transfer(path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'new')
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(path), before)
                self.check_history_replay(path, receipts)

    def test_replace_cannot_silently_destroy_collision_victims(self):
        statements = [
            """UPDATE OR REPLACE accounts SET rowid=(
                 SELECT rowid FROM accounts WHERE tenant='two' AND name='private')
               WHERE tenant='one' AND name='b'""",
            """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO accounts(rowid,tenant,name,balance)
               SELECT (SELECT rowid FROM accounts WHERE tenant='two' AND name='private'),
                 tenant,name,balance FROM accounts WHERE tenant='one' AND name='b'""",
            """UPDATE OR REPLACE transfers SET rowid=(
                 SELECT rowid FROM transfers WHERE tenant='two' AND key='past_two')
               WHERE tenant=NEW.tenant AND key=NEW.key""",
            """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO transfers(rowid,tenant,key,source,target,amount)
               SELECT (SELECT rowid FROM transfers WHERE tenant='two' AND key='past_two'),
                 tenant,key,source,target,amount FROM transfers
               WHERE tenant=NEW.tenant AND key=NEW.key""",
            """UPDATE OR REPLACE audit SET rowid=(
                 SELECT rowid FROM audit WHERE tenant='two' AND key='past_two')
               WHERE rowid=NEW.rowid""",
            """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO audit(rowid,tenant,key,source,target,amount)
               VALUES((SELECT rowid FROM audit WHERE tenant='two' AND key='past_two'),
                 NEW.tenant,NEW.key,NEW.source,NEW.target,NEW.amount);
               DELETE FROM audit WHERE rowid=NEW.rowid""",
        ]
        for index, statement in enumerate(statements):
            with self.subTest(statement=statement):
                path = self.new_db(f'replace-{index}')
                receipts = self.history(path)
                self.sql(f'CREATE TRIGGER fault AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN {statement}; END;', path)
                before = self.snapshot(path)
                with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.DatabaseError):
                    vault.transfer(path, 'one', 'a', 'b', 10, 'new')
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(path), before)
                self.check_history_replay(path, receipts)

    def test_ignored_writes_noops_and_rowid_moves_remain_valid(self):
        statements = [
            'UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance',
